summary: Covered how the deal team runs founder meetings from first contact to indicative offer. Agreed a standard first meeting guide, a five-criterion go or no-go screen and a 10 working day turnaround on indicative offers. Rolling the same coaching out to portfolio sales teams was turned down for now.

discussion.keyPoints: Each partner runs first meetings differently. Mark said notes are inconsistent and IC often asks questions that should have been covered at the first meeting.
The three objections that come up most are loss of control, how much debt goes on the business, and earn-outs. Helen said founders are wary after seeing other buy-outs over-leveraged.
Helen asked whether the same coaching could be given to portfolio company sales teams. Mark wanted to prove the approach on Calder's own deal team first.

recommendations.recommendation: Use a standard 12-question first meeting guide covering succession, management depth, customer concentration and growth plans.
Score every opportunity at first meeting against five criteria. Anything scoring below 3 does not go to IC.
Prepare written answers to the top three founder objections and state that leverage will not exceed 2.5x EBITDA.
Issue an indicative offer letter within 10 working days of the management meeting.
Run a monthly sales clinic led by Helen for the sales leads of all 7 portfolio companies.

actions.action: Write the 12-question first meeting guide and the five-criterion scoring sheet

nextFocus: Define pipeline stages and exit criteria using the new scoring screen.
nextPreparation: Bring the current deal log with dates of first meeting, offer and exclusivity for the last two years.

tests.question: What score does a deal need to go to IC?
How quickly should we issue indicative offer letters?
Did we agree the monthly sales clinic for portfolio companies?
